key_findings: Botai culture (3500 BCE) is earliest confirmed horse domestication site based on metrical + pathological + chemical evidence (3-evidence convergence is methodologically robust)
Western steppe horses dominated globally by 2000 BCE (genetic replacement documented)
Unresolved: single domestication (Botai sole origin) vs. dual domestication (Botai + Western steppe independent) — genetic continuity/discontinuity unclear

claims_consolidated.text: Horse domestication occurred at Botai culture, northern Kazakhstan, around 3500 BCE based on metrical analysis of horse remains

confidence_history.reason: Faz C flagged: Botai is oldest KNOWN site but other early domestication sites contested; 'sole origin' claim should be qualified as 'earliest known'
Red-team flag addressed: claim revised to 'earliest known/confirmed site' rather than implying sole origin

claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - requires production caveat: 'Botai (3500 BCE) is the earliest known evidence of horse domestication; whether it was the sole origin or one of multiple domestication events remains debated among geneticists'

claims_consolidated.text: Botai culture evidence includes three independent types: metrical analysis of metacarpals, pathological bridling marks, and mare's milk residues in pottery

confidence_history.reason: Converging independent evidence types methodologically sound; no revision needed

claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: READY - multi-modal evidence is high-quality; no qualification needed

claims_consolidated.text: Western Eurasian steppe (lower Volga-Don region) served as the homeland of modern domestic horses that spread globally from ~2000 BCE

confidence_history.reason: Red-team flag: 'replacement' is contested; introgression (wild-horse persistence/hybridization) documented in some regions. Claim overstates completeness of replacement
Global expansion pattern clear; regional variation (replacement vs. introgression) is normal; claim directionally sound but requires nuance about regional variation

claims_consolidated.d2_qualification: CONDITIONAL - requires caveat: 'Western steppe horses became dominant globally by 2000 BCE, though in some regions local wild-horse populations persisted or interbred rather than being completely replaced'

causal_links.effect_event: Western steppe horse expansion (2000 BCE, C-B1-003)

causal_reasoning.temporal_relationship: Clear: Botai 3500 BCE → Western steppe expansion 2000 BCE
causal_reasoning.mechanism: Unclear if Botai lineage directly leads to Western steppe dominance or if Western steppe represents independent domestication that outcompeted Botai — genetic continuity disputed
causal_reasoning.causal_evidence: Genetic data ambiguous; timing correlation only

causal_links.note: Genetic evidence shows replacement/dominance but not necessarily direct causal chain from Botai. Multiple domestication hypothesis increasingly plausible.

historiography.main_debate: Single-origin (Botai) vs. Multiple domestication events (Botai + Western steppe independent)

competing_schools.position: Botai culture (3500 BCE) is earliest known horse domestication, with morphological+pathological+chemical evidence
Modern domestic horses originated in Western Eurasian steppe and expanded globally; outcompeted local populations by 2000 BCE
Botai local domestication + Western steppe independent domestication; Western steppe lineage became dominant

unknowns.question: Were Botai and Western steppe horse domestications the same lineage or independent events?
competing_explanations: Single origin (Botai); Western steppe horses are Botai descendants
Dual domestication: independent; Western steppe proved superior
Botai horses replaced by Western steppe genetic introgression
